EC1: Administration of the licensed MF59-containing vaccines [OR], e.g. Fluad [OR] or Addigrip or virosome-based influenza vaccines such as Inflexal V [OR], InfectoVac Flu [OR] or Invivac during the 2006-2007 influenza season.
EC2: Administration of licensed vaccines within 2 weeks (for inactivated vaccines ) [OR] or 4 weeks (for live vaccines) prior to enrolment in this study.
EC3: Planned administration of a vaccine [OR] not foreseen by the study protocol [AND]  up to 30 days after the second vaccination [AND] with H5N1 vaccine.
EC4: Chronic administration (defined as more than 14 days) of immunosuppressants or other immune-modifying drugs within six months prior to the first administration of the study vaccine.
EC5: Any confirmed [OR] or suspected immunosuppressive [OR] or immunodeficient condition, based on medical history and physical examination (no laboratory testing required).
EC6: History of chronic alcohol consumption [OR] and/or drug abuse.
EC8: History of allergic [OR] disease or reactions likely to be exacerbated by any component of the vaccine (including egg and thiomersal allergy).
EC9: Acute clinically significant pulmonary [OR], cardiovascular [OR], hepatic [OR] or renal functional abnormality, as determined by physical examination or laboratory screening tests.
EC10: Acute disease at the time of enrolment.
EC11: Serious chronic disease including any medically significant chronic  pulmonary [OR], cardiovascular, renal, neurological, psychiatric [OR] or metabolic disorder, as determined by medical history and physical examination.
EC12: Administration of immunoglobulins [OR] and/or any blood products within the three months preceding the first vaccination [OR] or during the study.
EC13: Use of any investigational [OR] or non-registered product  (drug [OR] or vaccine) [AND] [NOT] other than the study vaccine(s) within 30 days prior to the first vaccination, or planned use during the study period.
EC14: Any condition which, [AND] in the opinion of the investigator, prevents the subject from participation in the study.
